SuttaCentral records no English translation title for the poem, though five modern translations across five languages are indexed [SuttaCentral]. No direct discussions of this text occur in the available secondary literature dossier.

SuttaCentral does not record any curated parallels in non-Pali corpora, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches meeting its threshold [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus records 33 internal Pali text-reuse matches across 13 works, reflecting standard Apadāna verse formulas [DharmaNexus]. The text shares extensive verse runs—particularly between segments §1.4 and §6.1—with other flower-offering verses in the Therāpadāna, including the immediately adjacent *Ekacampakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 370) and *Saḷalapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 372), as well as earlier poems such as *Piyālapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 239), *Saḷalapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 270), and *Ticampakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 256) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments §0.3–2.1 with passages in the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
